# lean-pkg list

static table, pipe-friendly.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg list [--only NAME[,NAME]] [--fields a,b,c] [--no-claims] [--json]
```

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--only NAME[,NAME]` | filters PACKAGES, never fields: only these packages (comma-separated names), each with its full record (cached claims included: --no-claims or --fields shrink it); the same table or --json shape, restricted; an unknown name exits 1 |
| `--fields a,b,c` | trims FIELDS, never packages: each package record cut to these keys, comma-separated; the same validation, dotted paths and aliases as `status --fields` (gate.receipt, lease.agent, lease.expires_at; the table columns as aliases: pin, vis, reaudit, expires; an unknown field exits 2 listing the valid keys); --json keeps the dump's shape plus a `fields` list, text prints the selected keys of each package as YAML |
| `--no-claims` | drop the bulk cached arrays (claims; the \[bulk] keys below) from each package record; every other key unchanged; --json adds an `omitted` list |

```text
  repo                  git URL (or local bare path) of the repository

  lean_toolchain        lean-toolchain detected in the checkout
  mathlib_pin           Mathlib revision from lake-manifest.json
  upstream_target       upstream goal: none | mathlib | palomar

  gate                  trust gate {receipt, comparator, axioms_allowed}: receipt paths in the repo

  reaudit_after         ISO date after which to re-audit, or null
  notes                 free text
  history               append-only event list (status prints the last 5; --json all)
  license_spdx          SPDX license id or expression, or null [v2]
  formalization_yaml    repo-relative path of formalization.yaml, or null [v2]
  palomar               Palomar evidence entries [{id, version, commit, comparator_config, ...}] [v2]
  doi                   {concept, versions[{doi, tag, commit, minted_at}]} or null [v2]
  reservoir             {listed_at, url} once Reservoir lists it, or null [v2]
  consent               consent records [{who, role, recorded_at, pointer}] [v2]
  claims_file           repo-relative path of the claims/1 file [v3]
  claims                cached claims from the last `claims sync` (can be hundreds of KB) [bulk] [v3]
  claims_synced_commit  40-hex commit the cached claims were read at, or null [v3]
  paper                 {arxiv, status} of the paper behind a paper-coupled package [optional]
  namespace_notes       {Lean root namespace: why sharing it with another package is intended} [optional]
  source_paper          {title, authors[], arxiv, doi} of the formalized paper (credited in formalization.yaml acknowledgements, never as project.authors) [optional]
  ai_assistance         {tools[], roles[]}: AI tools used and for what (rendered into acknowledgements) [optional]
  track                 DOI track: palomar | doi-only (absent = palomar); doi-only lets a public package record doi-minted without a palomar-* event (update --track) [optional]
  docs_descendants      true: a receipt bound to commit C is also accepted at a descendant of C where no build input under the package directory changed (docs-only rule, docs/receipts.md); absent = false (update --accept-docs-descendants) [optional]
  build_inputs          [glob]: extra package-relative paths the docs-only rule treats as build inputs (fnmatch; a glob without / also matches a basename) (update --build-inputs) [optional]
  headline_config       repo-relative path of the headline comparator configuration (the paper's main results; formalization.yaml status.main_results lists its theorems); absent = comparator.headline.json when tracked (update --headline-config) [optional]
  publication_hold      {reason, at, by}: the owner withdrew publication (update --withdraw-publication); promote refuses while it is set; only update --release-publication-hold lifts it [optional]
```

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | static table, script-friendly. `--only` filters packages, never fields: the table or the `--json` dump holds just the named packages, each with its full record, cached claims included (the dump's shape is unchanged: `version` plus `packages` holding just those records); an unknown name exits 1 like `status`. `--fields` trims fields, never packages: each package record is cut to those keys with the validation and dotted paths of `status --fields` (an unknown field exits 2 listing the valid keys); `--json` keeps the dump's shape and adds a `fields` list, text mode prints each package's selected keys as YAML instead of the table. Combine them for one value of one package: `list --json --only NAME --fields status`. `--no-claims` drops the bulk cached arrays, the keys tagged `[bulk]` in [Package record](../cli.md#package-record) (today `claims`), from each record and leaves every other key and the dump's shape unchanged; `--json` adds an `omitted` list naming them | `--json` `[--only NAME[,NAME]]` `[--fields a,b,c]` `[--no-claims]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `list` (exit 0): `packages`, `version`

## Examples

One line per package, for a terminal or a pipe.

```bash
lean-pkg list
```

Sample output:

```text
NAME      STATUS  VIS      LEASE  EXPIRES  PIN  REAUDIT
my-proof  active  private  -      -        -    -
```

One value of one package, as JSON for a script.

```bash
lean-pkg list --json --only my-proof --fields status
```
